prompts.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset: local Chinese history game for ages 4–6, a single landscape 3:2 storybook scene, rich painterly detail, no text or lettering. Reference images are ONLY for the established children's identities and warm hand-painted storybook style. Keep exactly the same three modern Chinese children: yellow jacket boy with spiky short black hair and no glasses, red/orange jacket girl with high ponytail and flower clip, green jacket boy with straight fringe and round clear glasses. Scene: a calm modern children's reading room, beside a small open antique-book exhibition case in the distant background. The kids are learning together: the yellow boy demonstrates clapping two hands gently; the girl attentively mirrors the hand motion; the green boy watches and then tries, a friendly adult guide in teal nearby. Expressions of curiosity and concentration, not a triumphant quiz celebration. Books and wooden study materials on a low table, warm sunlight, trees outside. Full faces and hands visible. Ancient book in background is purely illustrative, no readable invented Chinese, no claim of historical photograph. The scene illustrates children applying a saying from the Analects today, not Confucius personally teaching modern children. Keep the lower middle clear enough to observe actions, avoid confusing extra children, do not clone either boy's hair.

Use case: illustration-story. Asset: local Chinese history game for ages 4–6, a single landscape 3:2 illustrated scene. Reference images set ONLY the existing painterly children's-book style and character identities. Exactly three modern Chinese children: yellow jacket spiky-haired boy WITHOUT glasses, red/orange jacket ponytail girl with flower clip, green jacket straight-fringe boy WITH round clear glasses. In a warmly lit archaeological museum gallery, the three kids and a teal-clad adult guide observe Qin terracotta sculptures from OUTSIDE a low protective barrier. Show a standing terracotta figure and a kneeling terracotta archer sculpture with clearly different poses, and a terracotta horse deeper in the gallery. These sculptures have weathered earth/clay surfaces and are obviously museum objects, not living warriors. No weapons in the children's hands, no combat. Girl points at a bent knee; green boy notices rows of small armor plates; yellow boy compares the horse. Keep hands, faces and viewing subjects unobscured and entirely within frame. A separate distant conservator table may hint careful modern preservation but no touching by children. Rich warm watercolor-gouache textures and expressive recognizable friends, not cheap flat clipart. No text, signs, fake inscriptions, watermark or layout frames. This is a teaching story illustration, never a substitute for an actual artifact photograph.
